page_title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 3)

summary.title: Learning to Fly: Let's simulate evolution in Rust (pt 3)
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a generic genetic algorithm library in Rust, covering selection (roulette wheel), uniform crossover, and how to test randomized code using seeded RNGs and histograms.
keywords: how does a genetic algorithm work
takeaways: A genetic algorithm evolves a population by selecting parents by fitness, recombining their chromosomes with crossover, and mutating the results.
Roulette wheel (fitness proportionate) selection can be implemented with rand's choose_weighted, giving higher-fitness individuals more chances to be picked.
Uniform crossover mixes genes from two parent chromosomes at equal probability; the author checks this with a seeded RNG and counting differing genes.
Rust traits (SelectionMethod, CrossoverMethod, Individual) keep the library generic, and Index, FromIterator and IntoIterator make Chromosome easy to use.
summary.summary: This third part of the Learning to Fly series builds a generic genetic algorithm library in Rust, intended to evolve the weights of the neural network from the previous post. The author walks through the design decisions step by step: passing fitness as a trait method versus a closure, using a SelectionMethod trait, and implementing roulette wheel selection via rand's choose_weighted. Testing is handled with a hand-written TestIndividual struct and histograms over many seeded (ChaCha8) random draws, rather than mocks. The post then introduces a Chromosome type of f32 genes and a CrossoverMethod trait with a uniform crossover implementation, verified by checking that the child takes roughly 50/50 of its genes from each parent.
